title: Unconstrained Administrative SSH Commands (Missing ForceCommand)
damaged_code:
```text
# Inside authorized_keys configuration
ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2E... user@hostname
```
pattern: Granting remote support or automation processes full administrative shell access via SSH public keys without applying strict execution boundaries.
why_bad: An attacker who compromises the client's automated workstation inherits unlimited administrative permissions to execute arbitrary commands, format databases, or compromise other clusters on the target server.
detection: SSH public key entries inside production configurations that lack `command=` or `ForceCommand` parameters.
fix: Employ the SSH `ForceCommand` option or restrictive authorization keys configurations to constrain the administrative key to execute only a single, pre-defined, validated script.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 74-75.
